label: lem:admissible-patches
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:admissible-patches}
For every fixed \(b>0\), there are arbitrarily large system sizes
\(N=M\xi\), with \(M\) even, \(\xi=O_b(\log N)\), satisfying
Eq.~\eqref{eq:reference-design-condition} with
\(\varepsilon=N^{-b}\).
head: environment
name: Admissible logarithmic patch sizes

title: Proof
body_md:
Let \(M\) run over sufficiently large even integers and choose
\[
 \xi=\left\lceil4(1+b)\log_2 M+C_0+2\right\rceil,\qquad N=M\xi.
\]
For all sufficiently large \(M\), \(\xi\le M\): the ratio
\(\log M/M\) tends to zero, as follows for example from
\(\log x=\int_1^x u^{-1}du\le2\sqrt x\) for \(x\ge1\).
It follows that \(\log_2N\le2\log_2M\).  Hence
\[
 2\log_2(2N/N^{-b})+C_0
 =2+2(1+b)\log_2N+C_0
 \le 4(1+b)\log_2M+C_0+2
 \le\xi.
\]
Also \(\xi=O_b(\log M)=O_b(\log N)\), and \(N\) is unbounded.
head: environment

label: lem:haar-two-copy-audited
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Haar two-copy twirl, with its elementary commutant proof

title: Proof
body_md:
Haar invariance implies that the twirled operator commutes with
\(U\otimes U\) for every unitary \(U\).
We verify that this commutant is spanned by \(\mathbbm{1},F\).
Commutation with all diagonal phase matrices implies that its matrix
element \(\langle ij|Z|kl\rangle\) vanishes unless the multisets
\(\{i,j\}\) and \(\{k,l\}\) coincide.  To see this, vary each diagonal
phase independently; any nonzero difference of its two multiplicities
would change that matrix element by a nontrivial phase.
Commutation with all permutation matrices then makes all coefficients
of each of the three remaining types equal.  Consequently
\[
 Z=b\mathbbm{1}+cF+(a-b-c)\sum_i\ket{ii}\!\bra{ii}.
\]
A unitary taking \(\ket1\) to
\(\ket+=(\ket1+\ket2)/\sqrt2\) must take the eigenvector \(\ket{11}\),
of eigenvalue \(a\), to an eigenvector \(\ket{++}\) of the same
eigenvalue.  The coefficient of \(\ket{12}\) in \(Z\ket{++}\) is
\((b+c)/2\), while that in \(a\ket{++}\) is \(a/2\).
Thus \(a=b+c\), proving the commutant assertion.

Write the twirl as \(\alpha\mathbbm{1}+\beta F\).  Unitary invariance of trace,
and \(F(U\otimes U)=(U\otimes U)F\), give
\[
 D^2\alpha+D\beta=\operatorname{Tr} X,\qquad
 D\alpha+D^2\beta=\operatorname{Tr}(FX).
\]
Solving these two equations gives Eq.~\eqref{eq:haar-two-copy-audited}.
head: environment

label: lem:design-suppresses-phi
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:design-suppresses-phi}
Let \(S\) consist of \(s\ge1\) qubits, \(d=2^s\), \(q=d^2-1\),
and let \(O_1,\ldots,O_q\) be its embedded nonidentity Pauli basis.
Define
\[
 \varphi_S(U)=\frac1q\sum_a c_a(U),\qquad
 c_a(U)=D^{-1}\operatorname{Tr}(O_aUO_aU^\dagger).
\]
If \(\mathcal U\) has additive two-design error at most \(\varepsilon\),
then
\begin{align}
 \mathbb E_{\mathcal U}|\varphi_S(U)|^2
 &\le \frac1{q(D^2-1)}+\varepsilon,\label{eq:design-suppresses-phi}\\
 \left|\mathbb E_{\mathcal U}\varphi_S(U)\right|
 &\le\varepsilon.\label{eq:design-controls-first}
\end{align}
head: environment
name: Scalar autocorrelation at the reference time

label: eq:correct-two-copy-contraction
title: Proof
body_md:
Every \(c_a(U)\) is real because conjugating its trace and cycling the
two Hermitian factors leaves it unchanged.  Therefore the correct
two-copy representation is
\begin{equation}
 |\varphi_S(U)|^2
 =\frac1{q^2D^2}\sum_{a,b}
   \operatorname{Tr}\!\left[
    (O_a\otimes O_b)U^{\otimes2}
    (O_a\otimes O_b)U^{\dagger\otimes2}\right].
 \label{eq:correct-two-copy-contraction}
\end{equation}
For each pair \(a,b\),
\(\|O_a\otimes O_b\|_\infty=1\) and
\(\|O_a\otimes O_b\|_1=D^2\).
The two-design norm bound therefore changes the expectation of each
normalized summand by at most \(\varepsilon\).  Indeed,
\(|\operatorname{Tr} XY|\le\|X\|_\infty\|Y\|_1\): writing a singular-value
decomposition \(Y=\sum_j s_j\ket{u_j}\!\bra{v_j}\) bounds the trace by
\(\sum_j s_j|\langle v_j|X|u_j\rangle|
 \le\|X\|_\infty\sum_j s_j\).
Averaging over \(q^2\) pairs preserves the same error bound.

For the Haar value, \(\operatorname{Tr}(O_a\otimes O_b)=0\) and
\(\operatorname{Tr}[F(O_a\otimes O_b)]=\operatorname{Tr}(O_aO_b)=D\delta_{ab}\).
Using Eq.~\eqref{eq:haar-two-copy-audited} and contracting again with
\(O_a\otimes O_b\) gives
\[
 \mathbb E_{\rm Haar}c_a(U)c_b(U)=\frac{\delta_{ab}}{D^2-1}.
\]
Summation over \(a,b\) gives the Haar value \(1/[q(D^2-1)]\).

For the first moment, use instead
\[
 c_a(U)=D^{-2}\operatorname{Tr}\!\left[
 (O_a\otimes\mathbbm{1})U^{\otimes2}(O_a\otimes\mathbbm{1})U^{\dagger\otimes2}\right].
\]
The same norm estimate bounds its design error by \(\varepsilon\).
Both \(\operatorname{Tr}(O_a\otimes\mathbbm{1})\) and
\(\operatorname{Tr}[F(O_a\otimes\mathbbm{1})]\) vanish, so its Haar expectation is zero.
Averaging over \(a\) proves Eq.~\eqref{eq:design-controls-first}.
head: environment

label: lem:structural-frequencies
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Positive spectral representation and almost-sure frequency identification

title: Proof
body_md:
For each \(a\), summing squared matrix entries of \(VO_aV^\dagger\)
gives \(\operatorname{Tr}(O_a^\dagger O_a)=D\).  Thus the pair weights sum to one.
Expanding the normalized trace in the eigenbasis gives the pair
representation of \(\varphi_S\), and grouping pairs with equal vectors
gives Eq.~\eqref{eq:structured-phi}.

For \(\ell\ne\ell'\), choose a coordinate on which their difference is
nonzero.  Conditional on all other energies,
\((\ell-\ell')\cdot J=0\) fixes at most one value of that energy.
Absolute continuity makes its conditional probability zero.
There are finitely many pairs of vectors, so the union of these events
also has probability zero.  The same argument with \(\ell'=0\)
excludes additional zero frequencies.
The temporal identities now follow from
Lemma~\ref{lem:Cesaro-orthogonality}.  Distinct ordered pairs can still
have the same vector \(\ell\); their structural resonances have already
been included in \(W_\ell\).
head: environment

label: lem:reference-collision
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Reference phases measure the collision weight exactly

title: Proof
body_md:
For an integer \(k\) and \(J\) uniform on \([-1,1]\),
\[
 \mathbb E e^{-itkJ}=
 \begin{cases}\sin(kt)/(kt),&kt\ne0,\\1,&kt=0.\end{cases}
\]
At \(t=\pi\) this equals zero for nonzero \(k\).
Independence applied to Eq.~\eqref{eq:structured-phi} leaves just
\(\ell=0\) in the first moment.  In its squared modulus it leaves just
\(\ell=\ell'\), because all vector differences are integer.
This proves both identities.  Average over \(V\), apply
Theorem~\ref{thm:Cui-design-input} and
Lemma~\ref{lem:design-suppresses-phi}, and note \(W_0\ge0\).
The last assertion holds because \(W_\ell,\beta\) are functions of \(V\)
alone, not of any energy variables.
head: environment

label: lem:bounded-density-fourier
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:bounded-density-fourier}
Suppose a random energy has a probability density \(p\) on \([-1,1]\)
which is absolutely continuous there, with derivative in \(L^1\).
If
\[
 |p(-1)|+|p(1)|+\int_{-1}^{1}|p'(x)|dx\le L_0,
\]
then its characteristic function \(g(u)=\int_{-1}^{1}p(x)e^{-iux}dx\)
satisfies
\[
 |g(u)|\le\min\{1,L_0/|u|\}\quad(u\ne0).
\]
The uniform density has \(L_0=1\).
head: environment
name: Fourier estimate for bounded regular energy densities

title: Proof
body_md:
The bound by one follows from nonnegativity and normalization of \(p\).
For \(u\ne0\), integration by parts gives
\[
 g(u)=\left[\frac{p(x)e^{-iux}}{-iu}\right]_{-1}^{1}
       +\frac1{iu}\int_{-1}^{1}p'(x)e^{-iux}dx.
\]
Taking absolute values proves the stated estimate.
For \(p=1/2\), the boundary terms sum to one and the derivative vanishes.
head: environment

label: thm:scalar-dephasing
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: Scalar dephasing with no Hilbert-space or patch-count prefactor

title: Proof
body_md:
Expanding Eq.~\eqref{eq:structured-phi} gives
\[
 \mathbb E_J|\varphi_S(t)|^2
 =\sum_{\ell,\ell'}W_\ell W_{\ell'}
      \prod_{i,u}g_{i,u}\bigl(t(\ell_{i,u}-\ell'_{i,u})\bigr).
\]
For \(\ell=\ell'\), the product equals one and the corresponding sum is
\(\beta(V)\).  If \(\ell\ne\ell'\), choose a patch on which
\(m_{i,u}=\ell_{i,u}-\ell'_{i,u}\) is nonzero.  Each vector satisfies
\(\sum_u\ell_{i,u}=0\), so \(\sum_um_{i,u}=0\).
Therefore at least two coordinates of \(m\) are nonzero.  These
coordinates refer to independent energy variables; each nonzero integer
has modulus at least one.  For \(|t|>L_0\), at least two factors in
the product consequently have modulus at most \(L_0/|t|\), and all
remaining factors have modulus at most one.  For \(|t|\le L_0\) every
factor has modulus at most one.  The product is thus bounded by
\(r_{L_0}(t)\) in all cases.

The coefficients \(W_\ell W_{\ell'}\) are nonnegative.  Their sum over
\(\ell\ne\ell'\) is
\((\sum_\ell W_\ell)^2-\sum_\ell W_\ell^2=1-\beta(V)\).
Taking absolute values of this finite off-diagonal sum proves the first
inequality.

For \(\widetilde\varphi_S\), use
Lemma~\ref{lem:structural-frequencies} to restrict both indices to
nonzero vectors.  The diagonal sum is \(\beta-W_0^2\); the remaining
coefficients sum to
\[
 (1-W_0)^2-(\beta-W_0^2)\le1.
\]
The identical product estimate proves the second inequality.
The exceptional probability-zero set in that lemma does not change any
expectation.  Finally average over \(V\) and use
Eq.~\eqref{eq:plateau-design-bound}.

label: thm:generic-nearly-local-AS
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:generic-nearly-local-AS}
Assume the reference-design condition and the independent energy-density
hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:scalar-dephasing}.  Then for every \(T>0\),
\begin{align}
 \mathbb E A_S(T)&\le b_N+\frac{2L_0}{T},\\
 \mathbb E\mathcal A_S(T;H)&\le b_N+\frac{2L_0}{T},\\
 \mathbb E\mathcal F_S(T;H)&\le b_N+\frac{4L_0}{T},\\
 \mathbb E\mathscr E_H(T)
      \le\mathfrak c_d\left(b_N+\frac{4L_0}{T}\right).
 \label{eq:structured-every-window-main}
\end{align}
Moreover,
\[
 \mathbb E\pi_{0,S}\le\varepsilon,\qquad
 \mathbb E\pi_{0,S}^2\le\varepsilon.
\]
The expectation in Eq.~\eqref{eq:structured-every-window-main} is outside
both the starting-time supremum and the input supremum.
head: environment
name: Autocorrelation and every-window relaxation at rate \(b_N+1/T\

title: Proof
body_md:
For \(T\le L_0\), \(\int_0^T r_{L_0}(t)dt=T\le2L_0\).
For \(T>L_0\), direct integration gives
\[
 \int_0^T r_{L_0}(t)dt
 =L_0+L_0^2\left(\frac1{L_0}-\frac1T\right)
 =2L_0-\frac{L_0^2}{T}\le2L_0.
\]
All squared correlations are nonnegative and bounded by one, so
interchanging the finite time integral and expectation is justified.
Equation~\eqref{eq:scalar-dephasing-averaged} and the last integral
estimate prove the two rectangular bounds.  The triangular weight has
normalized integral one and is at most one, so the same argument with
its \(1/T\) normalization gives the third bound.
Apply Eq.~\eqref{eq:positive-kernel-full} for each individual
Hamiltonian \emph{before} taking expectation to obtain the last bound.

The zero-mode statements follow from
\(\pi_{0,S}=W_0\) almost surely,
Eq.~\eqref{eq:plateau-design-bound}, and \(0\le W_0^2\le W_0\le1\).

title: Proof

Substitute \(T=N^c\), \(D=2^N\), and
\(b_N=N^{-b}+1/[q(2^{2N}-1)]\) into

head: environment

label: prop:structured-short-time-lower
title: Proposition
head: environment
name: The \(1/T\) dependence is sharp for the every-window criterion

title: Proof
body_md:
Choose a pure subsystem input \(\rho_S\) and
\(\rho_0=\rho_S\otimes\mathbbm{1}_B/m\).
A term whose support misses \(S\) commutes with \(\rho_0\).
There are at most \(5s\) terms meeting \(S\), each of norm at most one,
by Proposition~\ref{prop:structured-scope}.  The triangle inequality and
\(\|A X\|_1\le\|A\|_\infty\|X\|_1\) therefore give
\[
 \|[H,\rho_0]\|_1
 \le\sum_{i:\,\operatorname{supp}h_i\cap S\ne\varnothing}
                 2\|h_i\|_\infty\|\rho_0\|_1
 \le10s.
\]
Unitary evolution satisfies
\([H,\rho(t)]=e^{-itH}[H,\rho_0]e^{itH}\).
Integrating its derivative thus gives
\(\|\rho(t)-\rho_0\|_1\le10s\,t\) for \(t\ge0\).

Partial trace contracts trace norm on Hermitian differences.
For completeness, if \(X=X_+-X_-\) is its positive/negative
spectral decomposition, positivity of partial trace and the triangle
inequality give
\[
 \|\operatorname{Tr}_BX\|_1
 \le\operatorname{Tr}(\operatorname{Tr}_BX_+)+\operatorname{Tr}(\operatorname{Tr}_BX_-)
 =\operatorname{Tr} X_++\operatorname{Tr} X_-=\|X\|_1.
\]
Hence \(D_{\mathrm{tr}}(\Phi_t(\rho_S),\rho_S)\le5s\,t\).
The eigenvalues of \(\rho_S-\mathbbm{1}_S/d\) are \(1-1/d\) and
\(d-1\) copies of \(-1/d\), so
\(D_{\mathrm{tr}}(\rho_S,\mathbbm{1}_S/d)=a_d\).
The triangle inequality yields
\[
 D_{\mathrm{tr}}(\Phi_t(\rho_S),\mathbbm{1}_S/d)\ge a_d-5s\,t.
\]
For \(0\le t\le t_*=a_d/(10s)\), this distance is at least \(a_d/2\).
Since \(t_*\le1\), the length-\(T\) window starting at zero contains this
whole interval whenever \(T\ge1\).  Its average squared error is
therefore at least \(t_*a_d^2/(4T)=a_d^3/(40sT)\).
This proves Eq.~\eqref{eq:structured-short-time-lower}.

For \(T\le N^b\), the plateau \(N^{-b}\) is at most \(1/T\).
The exponential Haar term is also at most \(1/T\) for sufficiently large
\(N\).  The upper bound in
Theorem~\ref{thm:generic-nearly-local-AS} is consequently
\(O_{s,b,L_0}(1/T)\); the lower bound just proved holds for every
realization and hence after expectation.
head: environment

label: cor:all-longer-windows
title: Corollary
head: environment
name: One event covers every longer window and every local input

title: Proof
body_md:
Write \(L=kT+r\), where \(k\ge1\) is an integer and \(0\le r<T\).
Split the integral of \(e_H\) into \(k\) complete windows and a final
interval of length \(r\).  The latter integral is at most that over the
length-\(T\) window starting at the same point, because \(e_H\ge0\).
Thus the whole integral is at most \((k+1)Tu\le2Lu\).
For \(L=T\), the definition gives \(Tu\) directly.
On the set in Eq.~\eqref{eq:common-good-times}, \(e_H(t)\ge\eta^2\).
Integrating this lower bound over that set proves the claim.
No union bound over a continuum of times or states is used.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
For a specified collection \(\mathcal S_N\) of at most \(N^r\)
subsystems of a fixed maximum size, a union bound applied to
Eq.~\eqref{eq:structured-high-probability} gives the corresponding
simultaneous statement with failure probability multiplied by \(N^r\).
For threshold \(N^{-a}\), the failure probability therefore tends
to zero whenever \(\min\{b,c\}>a+r\).  The maximum subsystem size
remains fixed.
head: environment
name: Several subsystems

label: thm:positive-kernel-stability
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: Perturbation stability without resolving microscopic gaps

title: Proof
body_md:
For \(t\ge0\), differentiating
\(e^{-i(t-s)H}e^{-isG}\) and integrating from \(s=0\) to \(s=t\)
gives
\[
 \|e^{-itH}-e^{-itG}\|_\infty\le t\|H-G\|_\infty.
\]
For negative \(t\) apply the same argument to the adjoints.
For an operator \(O\), inserting and subtracting
\(e^{-itG}Oe^{itH}\), and using unitary invariance of the
Hilbert--Schmidt norm, gives
\[
 \|e^{-itH}Oe^{itH}-e^{-itG}Oe^{itG}\|_{2,D}
 \le2\delta |t|\,\|O\|_{2,D}.
\]
Every basis element \(O_a\) has normalized Hilbert--Schmidt norm one.
Cauchy--Schwarz in the defining trace and averaging over \(a\) therefore
give
\[
 |\varphi_S(t;H)-\varphi_S(t;G)|\le2\delta|t|.
\]
It follows that
\(|\varphi_S(t;H)|^2\le2|\varphi_S(t;G)|^2+8\delta^2t^2\).
The normalized second moment of the triangular weight is
\[
 \frac1T\int_{-T}^{T}
  \left(1-\frac{|t|}{T}\right)t^2dt
 =\frac2T\left(\frac{T^3}{3}-\frac{T^3}{4}\right)=\frac{T^2}{6}.
\]
Consequently
\(\mathcal F_S(T;H)\le
2\mathcal F_S(T;G)+(4/3)\delta^2T^2\).
Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:positive-kernel-return}, then take expectations
and use Theorem~\ref{thm:generic-nearly-local-AS}.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
At \(T=N^c\) and \(\delta_N\le N^{-v}\), the perturbation term is
\(O(N^{-2(v-c)})\); it is small when \(v>c\).
A sum of at most \(C N\) bounded local perturbations, each of norm at
most \(\lambda_N\), meets this hypothesis with
\(\delta_N=C N\lambda_N\).
Thus sufficiently small noncommuting perturbations are allowed, but
their required strength vanishes with \(N\).
This is not a theorem for generic order-one noncommuting couplings.
The uniformity in the starting time comes from the positive-kernel
certificate, not from a Duhamel estimate at the possibly enormous
starting time \(t_0\).
head: environment
name: Scope of the stability result
